Duration constant

The safety window between major flesh-work you personally perform shrinks from a month to a week.

A body normally needs real time between one major procedure and the next — a month, whether the Butcher's grafting in a new bio-augment or you're personally unweaving a mutation out of someone's flesh — or the tissue won't take the strain. Under your hands that window shrinks to a week. Any patient you personally graft, remove a bio-augment from, or unweave a mutation from, yourself included, can undergo another such procedure from you again after only a week's rest instead of the usual month. This doesn't reduce any single procedure's own recovery time or a removal rite's own downtime — it only shortens how soon the next one can begin.
